page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-8 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs and 64.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, the hardware features 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The CPU cache architecture includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage options.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU capabilities, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring in the top 25% at 2928.59. Multi-core performance and memory bandwidth benchmarks generally fall within the average range, showing 11730.12 in stress-ng multi-core tests and a read-only large block memory bandwidth of 62.15 GB/sec. Cryptographic and compression operations perform steadily, as evidenced by a Passmark encryption score of 9278.94 and a single-threaded gzip compression speed of 28.36 GB/sec. For database workloads, the instance handles 8.97 million Redis SET operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c2d-highmem-8 provides a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core, making it a resource-dense option for memory-bound workloads without the overhead of excess compute cores. However, the lack of local NVMe storage and GPU accelerators limits its suitability for high-I/O databases or heavy machine learning training. The instance is best suited for memory-intensive applications, including medium-sized databases, caching layers, software compilation, and general-purpose web serving.
